panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Real patient posterior-anterior chest radiograph in female with X-linked agammaglobulinemia showing left lower lobe opacity, but opacity/bronchiectasis/sinus disease are not in allowed vocabulary which only contains absent/small tonsils and absent cervical lymph nodes; per rule 6 no vocabulary finding can be named so panel excluded. b: Real patient sagittal chest CT showing cylindrical bronchiectasis in lingula and left lower lobe in X-linked agammaglobulinemia, but this manifestation is not in allowed vocabulary; no absent tonsils/lymph nodes visible, so excluded. c: Real patient head CT showing bilateral mucosal thickening of maxillary sinuses in X-linked agammaglobulinemia, but sinus thickening is not in allowed vocabulary; no vocabulary finding can be named so excluded.

panels.figure_caption: Clinical radiology studies on the female patient with X-linked agammaglobulinemia. a Posterior-anterior chest radiography with left lower lobe opacity at presentation, b Sagittal view of chest computed tomography showing cylindrical bronchiectasis in the lingula and left lower lobe, c Computed tomography of the head showing bilateral mucosal thickening of the maxillary sinuses
in_text_mentions: This patient received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) replacement (0.5 g/kg every 4 weeks) and, there times per week oral azithromycin prophylaxis, 10 mg/kg orally for frequent pulmonary exacerbations. There was some reduction of her productive cough, and her rhinosinusitis has also improved after six months of therapy. Her IgG levels were normal with replacement therapy (Fig. 1).
